clue.text: Line three times added to The Waste Land spoiled fine work

indicators.note: something spoiled has been ruined and knocked out of shape, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line, written three times
the title of T. S. Eliot's poem, taken letter for letter
swell is an informal word for fine or excellent

explanation.surface: A critic complains that someone tacked lines onto Eliot's great poem and ruined a fine work.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of three Ls and THE WASTE LAND gives ALL'S WELL THAT END; SWELL for fine completes the title.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is the title of a Shakespeare comedy, so it is a literary work.

clue.text: Wrong smoking receptacle hotel's thrown out

indicators.note: something thrown out is ejected, so a letter is removed from the word

parts.note: a dish for cigarette ash
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A hotel guest is wrongly evicted for using an ashtray.
explanation.definitionFit: Astray means off the right course, so it serves as an adjective meaning wrong or amiss.

clue.text: Abhorrent to Holmes criminally hiding answer

indicators.note: hiding something means keeping it inside, so one piece is tucked within the other
acting criminally means behaving wrongly, so the letters go out of their proper order

parts.note: taken as written
the detective's name, taken letter for letter
A is the standard abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: Holmes finds someone abhorrent because they are concealing the answer to a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To' looks like a link between definition and wordplay, but its letters join HOLMES in the anagram, with the A for answer inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Loathsome describes something causing disgust, a direct synonym of abhorrent.

clue.text: Brandish blade ultimately slicing bananas

indicators.note: a knife slicing something cuts into it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: bananas is slang for crazy, as is wild

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the final letter of the word is used

parts.note: the last letter of blade

explanation.surface: A knife cuts through a bunch of bananas as someone brandishes it.
explanation.walkthrough: Bananas looks like fruit for the blade to slice, but it means crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: To wield a weapon is to hold and flourish it, the same action as brandishing.

clue.text: Large room close to fire and grill

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
an attic is a room under the roof

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its last letter is taken

parts.note: the final letter of fire

explanation.surface: A big room by the fire with a barbecue grill.
explanation.walkthrough: Grill looks like a cooking device but here means a grating.
explanation.definitionFit: A lattice is a crisscross framework of strips, the same structure as a grille or grill.

clue.text: Kill vampire? Neo looks like one!

parts.note: Neo is the setter, so speaking as Neo gives I'M
a vampire is famously white-faced, so to look like one is to be pale

explanation.surface: The setter jokes that with his pallor he might be mistaken for a vampire and staked.
explanation.walkthrough: Crossword setters often refer to themselves by their pseudonym, so Neo stands for I'M. The question mark flags that the definition is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Vampires are traditionally killed with a stake through the heart, so to impale one is to kill it.

clue.text: Joyce's style muddled more minds

indicators.note: something muddled is confused and jumbled, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: the two words taken as letters

explanation.surface: James Joyce's way of writing left readers more confused than ever.
explanation.definitionFit: James Joyce's experimental prose in Ulysses is a defining example of the literary movement of modernism.

clue.text: Almost over — over from the word go

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: above is a synonym for over
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Something nearly finished is suddenly started again from scratch.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated word does two different jobs: first a synonym, then the cricket abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Ab ovo is Latin for 'from the egg', meaning from the very beginning.

clue.text: External layer red with comet disintegrating

indicators.note: something disintegrating breaks into pieces that can be reassembled in a different order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A glowing red comet breaks up, shedding its outer layer.
explanation.definitionFit: The ectoderm is the outermost germ layer of an embryo, giving rise to skin and nerves.

clue.text: For burlesque go without an undergarment

indicators.note: without here means outside, so one word wraps around the others

parts.note: to have a go is to have a try
the indefinite article
a vest is a sleeveless undershirt in British usage

explanation.surface: A burlesque performer is advised to go on stage without underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but it means outside. In Britain a vest is worn under a shirt, not over it.
explanation.definitionFit: A travesty is a grotesque imitation, as is a burlesque, which mocks by exaggeration.

clue.text: Notice drivel written about one being skilled

parts.note: an ad is a notice, such as an advertisement

indicators.note: written about means set around, so the second word encloses the last piece

parts.note: rot means nonsense
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A reviewer notes that drivel written about a person can still be cleverly done.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit means clever and dexterous, a direct synonym of skilled.

clue.text: See 1 across
Bug concealed by Allan Pinkerton's beginners?

indicators.note: beginners are the starts of words, so only the opening letter of each is used

parts.note: hid is the past tense of hide
the first letters of the two names

explanation.surface: The famous detective agency founder hides a listening device.
explanation.walkthrough: With Pinkerton the detective, 'bug' suggests a listening device, but here it is an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: An aphid is a small sap-sucking insect, and bug is a common term for an insect.

clue.text: Novelist died after bringing female into Irish court

indicators.note: after places one piece at the end, behind the others
bringing something into a place carries it inside, so one piece is set within another

parts.note: IR is a standard abbreviation for Irish
she is the female pronoun
to court someone is to woo them
D is the abbreviation for died in genealogies

explanation.surface: A novelist died after a woman was brought into an Irish courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: Court looks like a law court but means to woo.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Isherwood was an English novelist, author of Goodbye to Berlin.

clue.text: Servile follower duke found in Dorset town

indicators.note: found in means located inside, so the letter sits within the place name

parts.note: Poole is a coastal town in Dorset, a county in southern England
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A duke's fawning attendant turns up in a seaside town in Dorset.
explanation.definitionFit: Poodle is an idiom for a lackey who obediently does another's bidding, like a pet dog.

clue.text: Boy upset runs away from little green man one spotted

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a lad is a boy

indicators.note: going away from something means leaving it, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: little green men are the cartoon picture of Martians
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A boy flees in panic from an alien that someone has spotted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One spotted' reads as 'one seen', but it is the definition: a dog with spots.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dalmatian is a dog breed known for its black or liver spots on a white coat.

clue.text: What Cockney trichologist may treat for nothing?

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker famously drops the opening aitch sound of words, so that letter is left out

parts.note: a hair specialist treats hair that is thinning
the dropped aitch of London speech

explanation.surface: A London hair specialist treating a balding client for free.
explanation.walkthrough: A trichologist is a specialist in hair and scalp problems. 'For nothing' looks like 'free of charge', but nothing alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin air is the idiom for nothingness, as in vanishing into thin air.

clue.text: Rejected ruling?

parts.note: surface reading: a legal decision that was turned down by a court or panel
setter's reading: a monarch who has given up reigning over the kingdom

explanation.walkthrough: Ruling looks like a noun, a judgement, but it is the verb: to rule as a king does.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch who abdicated formally renounced the throne, rejecting the job of reigning.

clue.text: See 1 across
Annoyed as essential to assimilate Latin

indicators.note: to assimilate something is to absorb it, so one piece is taken inside another

parts.note: something needed is essential
L is the abbreviation for Latin

explanation.surface: A student is irritated at having to absorb Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle someone is to provoke them, so needled means irritated or annoyed.

clue.text: Parliament's not wanting Liberal to make stand

indicators.note: not wanting something means doing without it, so that letter is removed

parts.note: the Dáil is the lower house of the Irish parliament, with the possessive S
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: Parliament refuses to let the Liberals take a stand.
explanation.walkthrough: Stand looks like a verb, take a position, but it is a noun: a raised platform.
explanation.definitionFit: A dais is a raised platform for speakers, a kind of stand.

clue.text: Clowning Buffalo Bill conserves mass and energy

indicators.note: something that conserves keeps things safe within it, so the outer word holds the others

parts.note: Buffalo Bill was William F. Cody, the Wild West showman
M is the symbol for mass in physics
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A Wild West showman clowns around while doing physics with mass and energy.
explanation.walkthrough: Mass and energy suggest Einstein's equation, but they are just the physics symbols.
explanation.definitionFit: Clowning is slapstick humour, a form of comedy.

clue.text: See 27
Politician from right working with computer

parts.note: a Mac is an Apple computer
R is the abbreviation for right
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A right-wing politician is busy at his computer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' lets the computer piece go in front of the others.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmanuel Macron is a French politician, President of France.

clue.text: An attribute not entirely visible in Chinese republic

indicators.note: something visible in a frame is seen inside it, so these pieces sit within another

parts.note: Sino- is the prefix meaning Chinese

indicators.note: not entirely means incomplete, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
a mark is a distinguishing attribute

explanation.surface: A feature only partly seen in China's People's Republic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chinese republic' reads as one phrase, but Chinese is wordplay and republic alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: San Marino is a tiny independent republic surrounded by Italy.

clue.text: Diana could be one among the Crenaeae

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters might form something else once rearranged

parts.note: the goddess's name, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: The goddess Diana might be counted among a group of nymphs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Crenaeae are the nymphs of springs and fountains, a class of water nymph in Greek myth.

clue.text: Boris's country cottage — I see rotter returning

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the letters are read from right to left

parts.note: ah is the exclamation of sudden understanding
a cad is a rotter, a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: Someone recognises a scoundrel coming back to Boris's country house.
explanation.walkthrough: Boris is a typical Russian name, signalling a Russian word; it need not be any particular Boris.
explanation.definitionFit: A dacha is a Russian country house or summer cottage.

clue.text: Belief in crusade is misplaced

indicators.note: in means contained within, so the letters lie inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: Faith in a holy war is wrongheaded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Misplaced' looks like an anagram signal, but it only supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Deism is the belief in a creator who does not intervene in the universe.

clue.text: Anger consuming team sent back for panacea

indicators.note: sent back means returned, so the combined letters are written in the opposite direction
consuming means swallowing, so one word takes the other inside it

parts.note: to rile is to anger
XI is eleven in Roman numerals, the size of a football or cricket team

explanation.surface: An angry team sent home is offered a cure-all.
explanation.walkthrough: Anger looks like a noun but is the verb rile.
explanation.definitionFit: An elixir is a supposed remedy for all ills, the same as a panacea.

clue.text: When rebuilt see it really protects Plains tribe magician

indicators.note: to protect something is to surround and shield it, so the anagram wraps around the tribe
something rebuilt is put together again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the three words taken as letters
the Crow are a Native American people of the Great Plains

explanation.surface: A tribal magician's trick seems truly protective when performed again.
explanation.definitionFit: Aleister Crowley was an English occultist who called his practice magick.

clue.text: Nick goes after the French cargo

indicators.note: goes after means follows, so that piece is placed at the end

parts.note: la is French for the, feminine
a ding is a small dent or nick

explanation.surface: Someone steals French goods.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick looks like a name or slang for steal, but it is a small dent.
explanation.definitionFit: Lading is the load carried by a ship, as in a bill of lading, so it means cargo.

clue.text: Goodness! Nimrod's wounded one following Achilles!

parts.note: my is an exclamation of surprise

indicators.note: something wounded is damaged and disfigured, so its letters are reshaped

parts.note: the name without its possessive S

explanation.surface: A shocked cry: the hunter Nimrod has been hurt while in Achilles' train.
explanation.walkthrough: Following looks like 'coming after', but it means being a follower.
explanation.definitionFit: The Myrmidons were the warriors who followed Achilles in the Trojan War.
